title: Jesse Charles, John Handy and blind Freddie
summary: News of clarinetists: Jesse Charles, John Handy at Tulane, and a blind harmonica player from Laplace.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yeah, some of them wanted to go back. I was talking to a guy today on the bus, Jesse Charles. Says he's trying to come back on clarinet. You saw him today? Yeah, he said he's been intending to phone you up. Said he might could get you a little.
What the old boy used to play so much clarinet that would sing bass at Louis?
Oh, he work at... John Handy. Yeah, he work at Tulane University. John Handy. Yeah. Handy, he work at Tulane University. Yeah. You think he can't play no more?
He can't play saxophone. He can't play clarinet now.
That's a good play, though. That's a good play, though. Yeah, he's a wild boy. That's a good play. That's a good play.
Yeah, he's a wild boy. He can play. The old blind boy should play good, too, but he doesn't give up blind Freddie.
Yeah. Yeah. He come from right down there. Born right there. Yeah.
He's from Laplace? Come from Laplace.
Born right not so far down that road there, on that side of the road.
He plays harmonica now. Yeah, he's a harmonica dog.
Yeah, he can play. But you can't talk to him, you know? He's got so funny, you can't talk to him. He hears all kind of voices and everything.
Well, Larry wanted me to bring him down there. I tried to get him down there. He told me to be there, but he never did show up.
Well, he said, I don't know. He was supposed to come out here once and play for some church. But he didn't come.
